papers.title: Converse symplectic interlacing via low-rank singular value perturbations
papers.abstract: The symplectic interlacing theorem states that the symplectic spectrum of a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix satisfies a $2k$-step interlacing relation with the symplectic spectrum of every $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix. We prove the converse in this paper. More precisely, given a positive global symplectic spectrum of size $n$ and a positive local symplectic spectrum of size $n-k$ satisfying the $2k$-step interlacing inequalities, we construct a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix having the prescribed global symplectic spectrum and a $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix of it having the prescribed local symplectic spectrum. Our main tool is a reduction of $s$-principal compression to a rank-$k$ singular value perturbation. In the context of the Gaussian quantum marginal problem, our result implies that the symplectic interlacing inequalities are not merely necessary conditions on Gaussian marginals, but are also the complete spectral compatibility conditions for the global-versus-local-mode marginal problem.

papers.title: Boundary Geometry Determines Optimal Shallow ReLU Approximation under Weighted Coefficient Constraints
papers.abstract: We study how boundary geometry affects $L^q$ approximation by shallow ReLU neural networks on convex bodies $K\subset\mathbb R^d$. The target classes are unit balls of weighted variation spaces that can enlarge classical spaces by incorporating domain geometry into constraints on output coefficients. We establish upper and lower bounds for arbitrary convex bodies and determine the optimal polynomial approximation exponents for all planar convex bodies and their products with polytopes, including cubes and circular cylinders. For $C^2$ convex bodies, we determine the optimal exponents in a dimension-dependent range of $q$ extending beyond $2$. When all principal curvatures are positive, the result extends to every finite $q\ge2$. For these classes, the dependence of the optimal exponent on the domain is captured by a single geometric growth exponent associated with small boundary caps. We also identify sharp weight thresholds for retaining the classical approximation exponent and improve previous weights on Euclidean balls while preserving the classical $L^2$ approximation rate. When the target is given as a finite ReLU network, the upper bounds can be realized by a compressed network using only the original neurons, without increasing the weighted coefficient sum. These results show that boundary geometry can change the optimal exponent even when dimension, error norm, and weighting rule are fixed.

papers.title: On the Luxemburg Functional in the Concave Regime with an Application to Nonlocal Differential Equations
papers.abstract: For $p:[0,1]\to(0,1)$ a continuous function, we consider the Luxemburg functional \[ \Lambda_{p(\cdot)}(u):=\inf\left\{\delta>0:\int_0^1\left|\frac{u(t)}{\delta}\right|^{p(t)}\,dt\leq 1\right\}. \] We develop a suitable functional analytic framework for $\Lambda_{p(\cdot)}$ so that it can be incorporated into a positive order cone, which can then be used in the analysis of nonlocal differential equations having the general form \[ -A\left(\int_0^1 b(1-s)(u(s))^{p(s)}\,ds\right)u''(t) =\lambda f(t,u(t)),\qquad t\in(0,1). \] By means of a specific numerical example, we demonstrate that, as opposed to a methodology relying only on the supremum norm, our methodology via the Luxemburg functional yields an appreciably sharper localisation of any solutions of the nonlocal equation.

papers.title: A fractional modular Poincar\'e--Wirtinger-type inequality in Sobolev spaces with variable exponents
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain and let $p:\Omega\to[1,\infty)$ be a measurable, essentially bounded exponent; no regularity of $p$ -- in particular, no log-H\"older continuity -- is assumed. For a general non-negative measurable kernel $\mathcal{K}(x,y)$ admitting a radial bounding function $\kappa(x,r)$ in the second variable, we establish the fractional modular Poincar\'e--Wirtinger-type inequality $$ \iint_{\Omega\times\Omega}\mathcal{K}(x,y)\,|u(x)-u(y)|^{p(x)} d y\, d x \leqslant C\int_\Omega c(x)\left(\int_\Omega \frac{|\nabla u(z)|^{p(x)}}{|z-x|^{n-1+\theta}}\, d z\right) d x, $$ valid for every $u\in W^{1,1}(\Omega)$, in particular every $u\in W^{1,p(\cdot)}(\Omega)$, and every $\theta\in[0,1)$. Here $$ c(x)=\int_0^{D}r^{n+p(x)-2+\theta}\kappa(x,r)\,d r, $$ $D$ is the diameter of any fixed ball containing $\overline\Omega$, and the constant $C$ depends only on $n,p^+,\theta$ and the fixed domain $\Omega$. For the fractional kernel $\mathcal{K}(x,y)=|x-y|^{-n-\lambda p(x)}$ we obtain a variable-exponent Gagliardo-modular estimate. The proof replaces the starshaped chain decompositions used there by a combination of a Morrey-type estimate on starshaped domains, a positive-kernel proof of weighted Poincar\'e inequalities, and one reflection extension for the weights $|z-x|^{-(n-1+\theta)}$. The constants are uniform down to exponent $1$, and the inequalities are understood in the extended nonnegative sense when either side is infinite.

papers.title: A Counterexample to a Bourgain-Brezis Sum-Space Estimate
papers.abstract: A question of Bourgain and Brezis, later restated as Open Problem 7.1 by Brezis, asks whether the $H^{1/2}+W^{1,1}$ norm of a mean-zero scalar function is controlled by the ambient $H^{-1/2}+L^1$ sum norm of its gradient. We show that this estimate fails in every dimension $N\geq 2$. More precisely, for every integer $K\geq 16$, we construct a smooth real-valued mean-zero function $\Phi_K$ on $\mathbb{T}^N$ such that $|\nabla\Phi_K|{H^{-1/2}(\mathbb{T}^N)+L^1(\mathbb{T}^N)}\leq C$ and $|\Phi_K|{H^{1/2}(\mathbb{T}^N)+W^{1,1}(\mathbb{T}^N)}\geq cK^{1/4}-C$, where the absolute constants $c,C>0$ are independent of $N$ and $K$. Equivalently, the ratio of the gradient-constrained decomposition cost to the ambient decomposition cost is unbounded. The construction applies the Hodge projection to a smooth approximation of a normal vector measure on a codimension-one sheet. Its potential records lacunary partial sums at geometrically separated distances from the sheet. A scale-path lower bound, combined with an odd critical Hardy inequality, excludes uniformly bounded $H^{1/2}+W^{1,1}$ decompositions.

papers.title: Applications of the fixed point theorem for mappings contracting perimeters of triangles: ODEs, PDEs, integer and difference equations
papers.abstract: Mappings contracting perimeters of triangles are Banach contractions whenever every point of the underlying metric space is an accumulation point. Consequently, applying the perimeter-contraction theorem on a complete metric space without isolated points yields an existence result already covered by Banach's fixed point theorem. This observation applies, in particular, to operators associated with differential and integral equations acting on standard nontrivial function spaces, such as spaces of continuous functions $C[a,b]$, Lebesgue spaces $L_p$, and Sobolev spaces $W^{k,p}$, equipped with their usual norm metrics. Thus, applications extending beyond Banach's theorem for the same operator and metric require a complete invariant domain containing some number of isolated points. Such a domain may be a closed subset of a standard function space, despite the absence of isolated points in the ambient space. The main goal of this paper is to illustrate applications of the fixed point theorem for mappings contracting perimeters of triangles in settings where the associated operators are not Banach contractions. The differential-equation examples admit interpretations as stylized models combining continuous evolution, nonlocal measurement, and quantized feedback. The integer and difference-equation examples illustrate the effects of rounding on equilibria and periodic responses.

papers.title: Sharp Stability of Brenier Potentials and its Link to Poincar\'e Inequalities
papers.abstract: We prove a new functional inequality for uniformly log-concave measures, stronger than the Poincar\'e inequality. This new inequality bounds the variance of differences of convex functions and is motivated by the stability theory of optimal transport: for a fixed uniformly log-concave source measure, it provides a sharp stability bound for Brenier potentials with respect to variations of the target measure. Applying this inequality to Gaussian measures, we recover the fact that the Bures-Wasserstein distance between two positive semidefinite matrices is equivalent to the Frobenius distance between their square roots. Our proofs hinge upon linearization arguments for the Monge-Amp\`ere equation governing the quadratic optimal transport problem.

papers.title: A functional model for hyponormal contractions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish an analytical model for a class of hyponormal contractions $T$ satisfying $Ran[T^*,T] \subseteq \mathcal D_{T^*}\ominus \mathcal D_T$, where $\mathcal D_{T^*}$ and $\mathcal D_T$ are the associated defect spaces for $T$. We also show that, under a certain condition, a contraction $T$ with $\mathcal D_T \subseteq \mathcal D_{T^*}$ is hyponormal.

papers.title: Quaternionic Buzano-Dragomir Inequality and Deutsch Entropic Uncertainty Principle
papers.abstract: We show that the Buzano-Dragomir inequality holds for quaternionic Hilbert spaces. Using this generalization, we derive the Dragomir inequality for the quaternionic numerical radius and Deutsch entropic uncertainty principle for quaternionic Hilbert spaces.

papers.title: Exact $L^2$ convergence through the wavelet and tent space characterizations of $h^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$, $0<p\le 1$
papers.abstract: We extend the wavelet and tent space characterization of $h^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$ to $0<p\le 1$ via a local dyadic tent space $t_p$, and derive the unconditional $L^2$-convergence of the resulting atomic decomposition, with an exact error identity refining Ding, Jiang and Zhu (2019).

papers.title: Observable diameter of product measures with a power-type interior zero
papers.abstract: We determine the asymptotic order of the observable diameter of $\ell^p$-product spaces associated with a probability measure on $[0,1]$ whose density has a power-type interior zero. Different vanishing orders are allowed on the two sides of the zero. For every $1 \le p \le \infty$, we obtain sharp two-sided estimates and show that the asymptotic order is governed by the larger of the two vanishing orders. In the case $p=2$, the transition occurs exactly at the threshold for the spectral gap.

papers.title: Algebraic properties of Truncated Toeplitz $+$ Truncated Hankel operators
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the algebraic properties of $\mathcal{S}_\theta$---the class of truncated Toeplitz plus truncated Hankel operators --- on the model space $\mathcal{K}_\theta$. We also give a complete characterization of the intersection class of truncated Toeplitz and truncated Hankel operators under certain conditions. As applications, we describe the non-uniqueness of a decomposition $T=A+B$, show that self-adjoint operators admit self-adjoint decompositions, give a necessary and sufficient inclusion criterion for $\mathcal{S}_\theta$ when $\theta$ is a finite Blaschke product, and, from a first-order commutator characterization of $\mathcal{S}_\theta$, describe the products of its elements and the operators commuting with $S_\theta+ S_\theta^{*}$.

papers.title: Character cyclic amenability of Banach algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce and study the notion of character cyclic amenability for Banach algebras, which combines the cyclicity condition on derivations with the character-dependent module structure arising in character amenability. We establish several basic properties of this notion and investigate its behavior under standard Banach algebra constructions. In particular, we study character cyclic amenability for opposite algebras, projective tensor products, l1-direct sums, quotient algebras, dense homomorphic images, and theta-Lau products. We also provide examples illustrating the relationship between character cyclic amenability and other amenability-type properties, including examples showing that character cyclic amenability does not imply cyclic amenability. Finally, we characterize character cyclic amenability for module extension Banach algebras in terms of phi-cyclic derivations and derivations associated with the underlying Banach module.

papers.title: On families of copulas and quasi-copulas homeomorphic to the Hilbert cube and related results
papers.abstract: Working with tools from infinite-dimensional topology and using measure-theoretic ideas we analyze numerous well-known fami\-lies of copu\-las and quasi-copulas from a topological perspective, prove that most of them are homeomorphic to the Hilbert cube $\mathcal{H}$ and hence have the Fixed Point as well as the Disjoint Cells property. Working with so-called $Z$-sets, we then study how large one set is within another. Doing so, in order to show that a set $A$ is small/topologically negligible within a compact metric space $(\Omega,m)$, we construct a homeomorphism $h: [0,1] \times \mathcal{H} \to \Omega$ mapping $\{0\} \times \mathcal{H}$ to $A$. The obtained results are to a certain extent surprising since various supposedly small families are topologically large.

papers.title: Kwapie\'n's property (K) in Lipschitz-free spaces
papers.abstract: We prove that a Lipschitz-free space $\F(M)$ fails Kwapie\'n's property (K) whenever its underlying metric space $M$ contains a bi-Lipschitz copy of $C\times K$, where $C\subset\R$ is closed with positive measure and $K$ contains a Cantor metric space. Consequently, this holds for every subset of $\R^n$, $n\geqslant2$, whose closure has positive measure, and for a compact planar set of Assouad dimension one. These Lipschitz-free spaces embed into no strongly weakly compactly generated space and no $L_1$-space; in the separable case their duals are not isomorphic to $\ell_\infty$. Combining our result with a decomposition of Aliaga and Medina, we show that $\F(\R^n\times\Z^m)$ is strongly weakly compactly generated if and only if it has (K), and this occurs precisely when $n\leqslant1$. In particular, $\F(\R^2)$ does not embed isomorphically into $\F(\R\times\Z)$, answering a question of Aliaga. The planar examples nevertheless have the Dunford--Pettis property and Pe{\l}czy\'nski's property $(V^*)$ and are weakly sequentially complete.

papers.title: Finite-Branch Multipliers on a H\"older Algebra: Commutants, Norm Closures, and Essential Spectra
papers.abstract: Noninjective multiplication symbols allow commuting operators to mix function values along their fibers, while H\"older regularity constrains this mixing at branch points. We study these operators on the Banach algebra $A_\beta$, $0<\beta<1$, defined by a restricted interval-variation condition. For $u(t)=t(1-t)$, we determine the full commutant $\{M_u\}'=\mathscr C_\beta$, including operators whose reflection coefficients need not belong to $A_\beta$. Separately, we characterize the operator-norm closure $J_\beta$ of the regular multiplication--reflection subalgebra of $\mathscr C_\beta$, obtain two-sided norm-distance estimates, and find a complemented copy of $\ell^\infty/c_0$ in the Banach-space quotient $\mathscr C_\beta/J_\beta$. Every $T\in\mathscr C_\beta$ satisfies $\sigma(T)=\sigma_{\mathrm{ap}}(T)=\sigma_{\mathrm{usf}}(T)=\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(T)$, and Fredholmness is equivalent to invertibility. For multipliers with finitely many full bi-Lipschitz branches, we also characterize their full commutants and establish the same spectral equalities for every commuting operator. For the regular finite-branch algebra, we establish an exact norm-closure criterion using weighted local H\"older defects and separate row-difference conditions, even when several folds share a level.

papers.title: An $L^p$ Version of Raeburn's Symmetric Imprimitivity Theorem
papers.abstract: Let $1\leq p<\infty$. We prove an $L^p$-operator analogue of Raeburn's symmetric imprimitivity theorem for countable discrete groups. Let $A$ be an $L^p$-operator algebra with a contractive two-sided approximate identity, admitting a nondegenerate isometric representation on a $\sigma$-finite $L^p$-space. Given commuting free and proper actions of groups $G$ and $H$ on a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff space $Z$, together with commuting isometric actions on $A$, we show that the two corresponding full crossed products, and likewise the two reduced crossed products, are Morita equivalent as Banach algebras. The proof is organized through the linking groupoid. Its main analytic ingredient is a coefficient-valued spatial matrix dilation; in the reduced case we prove that this dilation preserves regularity after a Borel reindexing of the opposite corner. A pairing-valued approximate identity yields fullness and nondegeneracy.

papers.title: A Bounded Closed Convex Set in $c_0(\mathbb{C})$ without Modulus Support Functionals
papers.abstract: We construct a bounded closed convex set in $c_0(\mathbb{C})$ on which no nonzero continuous complex-linear functional attains its maximum modulus. Consequently, this answers in the negative the two longstanding questions raised by Deville, Godefroy and Zizler in \cite[p. 35]{DGZ}. The construction uses a small perturbation of the identity on $c_0(\mathbb{R})$.

papers.title: Rigidity of Exact Contractivity in the Complex Polynomial Bohnenblust--Hille Inequality
papers.abstract: The complex polynomial Bohnenblust--Hille inequality bounds the coefficient $\ell_{2m/(m+1)}$ norm of a complex $m$-homogeneous polynomial by its supremum norm, with a constant independent of the number of variables. For each fixed integer $N\ge3$, we characterize the choices of $N$ degree-$m$ monomials for which the inequality holds with optimal constant $1$ for every polynomial supported on them, provided $m$ exceeds an explicit threshold depending only on $N$. This holds precisely when their exponent vectors contain no nontrivial three-term arithmetic progression; equality for a nonzero polynomial then holds only for monomials. We also prove that, in the same degree range, every polynomial with at most $N$ nonzero coefficients that violates the constant-one inequality has a unique coefficient of maximal modulus, whose exponent is the center of such a progression in its support. Exact contractivity also follows from a comparability condition on the two largest coefficients, with a degree threshold that necessarily depends on the number of nonzero monomials.

papers.title: The sharp exponent for the Banach--Mazur distance to the cube
papers.abstract: Let $R_\infty(n)$ be the maximal Banach--Mazur distance from an $n$-dimensional real normed space to $\ell_\infty^n$. We prove that $R_\infty(n)\ge cn^{2/3}(\log(2n))^{-10}$. Together with the upper bound of Friedland, Naor, and Youssef, this gives $R_\infty(n) = n^{2/3+o(1)}$. The examples are polars of symmetric Gaussian polytopes with $2n$ generators, and the lower bound holds with exponentially high probability. A joint minimization over coefficient representations and positive weights yields an exact second-variation identity and sparse coefficients. A Gaussian projection argument controls all low-rank completions of the recorded matrix. An adaptive choice of exceptional generators then reduces the remaining case to a fixed-shift Gaussian small-ball estimate over two finite nets.

papers.title: A characterization of equality between de Branges--Rovnyak and Dirichlet spaces
papers.abstract: We characterize when a de Branges--Rovnyak space coincides with a harmonically weighted Dirichlet space. We obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for this identification, which settles a long-standing open problem. We illustrate the result with several examples, that include measures supported on uncountable sets.

papers.title: Characterization of Fourier transform of Hilbert space Valued functions
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to obtain the characterization of Fourier transform for functions taking values in a separable Hilbert space $H$, defined on the groups $G=\R^n,\,G=\Z/n\Z$. In the first part of the paper, we consider the Fourier transform as a bijective mapping on $S_H$, the space of all $H$-valued smooth rapidly decaying functions on $\R^n$, which naturally extends bijectively to the dual space $S_H'$. Within this framework, we characterize the Fourier transform in terms of the convolution theorem, supplemented by additional structural properties of the Fourier transform. In the second part of the paper, we consider the discrete setting, where the Fourier transform is an operator on $L^1(\Z/n\Z, H)$, and we provide corresponding characterization based on its essential properties. In contrast to the classical setting, a key assumption in our framework involves the interplay between two distinct convolution operations. As a consequence, the structure of our proof diverges notably from the classical case and introduces additional complexities.

papers.title: The Beurling-type theorem for powers of weighted Bergman shifts
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{B}_{\alpha}$ denote the shift operator on the weighted Bergman space $A^2_\alpha(\mathbb{D})$. We prove that, for every integer $k\geq1$, the Beurling-type theorem holds for $\mathcal{B}_{\alpha}^k$ on $A^2_\alpha(\mathbb{D})$ if and only if $-1<\alpha\leq1$. We also show that, for every $\alpha>-1$, there exists a finite Blaschke product $B$ such that $M_{B}$ admits a cyclic invariant subspace but fails the wandering subspace property.

papers.title: On Some Lie Group Invariant noncommutative functions
papers.abstract: We study noncommutative polynomials and functions invariant under linear actions of infinite (compact Lie) groups, with a focus on $SU(2)$ acting on two noncommuting variables. For $SU(2)$, we give a complete description of the invariant noncommutative polynomials: there are no invariants of odd degree, and in degree $2n$ the invariants are exactly the span of the $S_{2n}$-orbit of $(XY-YX)^n$. We also construct an explicit basis recursively from the operation $(A,B)\mapsto XAYB-YAXB$, and show that the space of degree-$2n$ invariants has dimension equal to the $n$-th Catalan number. All proofs proceed by direct computation with the Haar integral.

papers.title: A note on the Besov spaces ${\rm B}_1^{\Phi_2}$
papers.abstract: Regarding the Besov space ${\rm B}_1^{\Phi_2}$, defined by S. Geiss and Ylinen (Memoirs AMS 1335, 2021) by a coupling method, we prove for $\xi\in{\rm B}_1^{\Phi_2} \cap L_2$ a distributional estimate in terms of the Lorentz-Zygmund space $L_{1,\infty}(\ln L)^{-1}$ for the Malliavin derivative ${\rm D}(T_u\xi)$ uniformly in $u>0$, where $(T_u)_{u\ge }$ is the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semi-group. Here $\xi$ is not necessarily Malliavin differentiable in the ${\rm D}_{1,1}$-sense. This provides for Theorem 4.22 of the aforementioned reference an extension to the borderline case $p=1$.

papers.title: Actions of acylindrically hyperbolic groups on $\ell^1$
papers.abstract: We construct explicit affine uniformly Lipschitz actions on $\ell^1$ for certain groups with hyperbolic features. For acylindrically hyperbolic groups, our actions have unbounded orbits, while for residually finite hyperbolic groups and for mapping class groups, the actions have proper orbits, with the induced $\ell^1$-metric quasi-isometric (respectively, almost quasi-isometric, up to a logarithmic factor) to the word metric. This allows us to construct proper continuous affine uniformly Lipschitz actions on $L^1$, with undistorted orbits, for all simple groups of real rank one.

papers.title: Foundations of Double Operator Integrals with a Variant Approach to the Nonseparable Case
papers.abstract: We aim to give a self-contained and detailed yet simplified account of the foundations of the theory of double operator integrals, in order to provide an accessible entry point to the theory. We make two new contributions to these foundations: (1) a new proof of the existence of the product of two projection-valued measures, which allows for the definition of the double operator integral for Hilbert-Schmidt operators, and (2) a variant approach to the integral projective tensor product on arbitrary (not necessarily separable) Hilbert spaces using a somewhat more explicit norm than has previously been given. We prove the Daletskii-Krein formula for strongly differentiable perturbations of a densely-defined self-adjoint operator and conclude by reviewing an application of the theory to quantum statistical mechanics.

papers.title: Hyperbolicity Beyond Convexity in the Alexandrov-Fenchel Inequality
papers.abstract: We establish an Alexandrov--Fenchel type inequality in which one of the reference bodies is replaced by a function whose Hessian satisfies a balancing condition on its eigenvalues, without being required to be positive semidefinite. The proof hinges on a new extension of Alexandrov's inequality for mixed discriminants. As applications, we derive a log-concavity principle for linear functionals of area measures, answering a question of Colesanti, Hug, and Saor\'in-G\'omez, as well as Brunn--Minkowski type inequalities for intrinsic volumes of mean section bodies, answering a question of Schuster.

papers.title: An Ellipse Criterion for Exact Nonuniqueness in the Planar Interior Radon Problem
papers.abstract: We characterize exact nonuniqueness in the planar interior Radon problem for arbitrary pairs of open convex sets. There exists a nonzero smooth function compactly supported in the first set whose integral over every line meeting the second set vanishes if and only if an ellipse contains the closure of the second set and is compactly contained in the first set. The same criterion holds for a nonzero $L^1$ function whose essential support is compactly contained in the first set and whose Radon transform vanishes almost everywhere on those lines. For concentric open squares, the criterion gives the sharp threshold $1/\sqrt2$ for the inner-to-outer half-side ratio. This yields counterexamples to Conjecture 1.2 of Boman (2021) and to Theorem 40.1 of Boman (2025).

papers.title: A Framework for Supervised and Unsupervised Learning via Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces
papers.abstract: We introduce a unified framework for supervised and unsupervised learning through density estimation using reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHSs). To this end, we introduce the notion of a nested RKHS, that is, an increasing sequence of RKHSs whose union is dense in an ambient $L^2$-space. This construction allows us to exploit the computational structure of RKHS methods at each finite approximation level while preserving the approximation power of the entire $L^2$-space. We first study statistical learning in a fixed RKHS. In both unsupervised and supervised settings, we establish strong convergence results for empirical averages of random elements taking values in an RKHS continuously embedded in $L^2$. We then use the nested RKHS structure to combine these statistical convergence results with the density of the union of the RKHSs in the ambient $L^2$-space. We apply this construction to probability density estimation and binary Bayesian classification. For density estimation, we construct explicit empirical estimators of the orthogonal projections of the target density onto the RKHSs and establish their almost sure convergence. A diagonal selection procedure then yields a sequence of estimators converging almost surely to the target density in $L^2$. For binary Bayesian classification, we formulate the approximation of the Bayes target as the minimization of suitable population and empirical risk functionals. We prove consistency of the empirical minimizers and use the nested structure to obtain convergence towards the Bayes target in $L^2$. We further provide a geometric interpretation in terms of hyperplanes and weighted distances in the ambient $L^2$-space. Finally, we show that the population risk admits a direct probabilistic interpretation in terms of the probability of misclassification.
